narrative.overview: Kiuna AI reads like the control panel of a plant that already runs on IA: a flat, gray-blue daylight surface, thick ink-colored borders, and a single safety-orange accent reserved for what's live or actionable. The referent is physical signage — an industrial control board, floor markings, shift-change status boards — not a SaaS dashboard and not the previous dark theme. Elevation is flat (hard offset shadows, no blur/glow), typography splits between the sans body face and a monospace face reserved for module IDs and step numerals, and the bubble/spark particle motion carries over from the previous system, recolored to ink/safety/steel. This is a captured baseline of the current implementation, not a locked mandate — PRODUCT.md gives explicit permission to keep reinventing it if a change moves the site further from generic AI-SaaS territory.
keyCharacteristics: Flat daylight panel background (#e9edee) with white module surfaces and near-black ink text/borders — no gradients.
One-accent discipline: safety orange (#ff5a1f) marks only what's live, actionable, or proven.
One monospace face reserved for module IDs, step numerals, and REF.0x differentiator tags.
Thick (2px) ink-colored borders, small radii; no glass/blur chrome anywhere.
Flat elevation: hard offset shadow, never colored glow.
The 01–04 numeral motif is deliberately varied per content group instead of repeated identically.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Only safety orange carries interactive/live color meaning. No second accent color is introduced without renaming this rule.

rules.name: The One-Monospace Rule
rules.body: The monospace stack appears only on numerals/IDs/references: module IDs, step-number badges, REF.0x tags, vertical index chips, status tag, proof numbers. Every other character on the page is Aptos.

rules.name: The Varied-Index Rule
rules.body: The 01-04 numeral motif does not repeat the same treatment across unrelated content groups: Verticales use a filled module-plate chip, Proceso uses a circular node on the connector line, Diferenciadores use a small REF.0x label with no large numeral.

rules.name: The Flat-Elevation Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no colored glow, no gradient panel fill. Elevation comes from the single Flat Offset shadow and/or a thicker ink border.

dos: Do keep the One-Accent Rule: safety orange only for what's live/actionable/proven.
Do keep the monospace face restricted to numerals/IDs/references.
Do keep the three numeral treatments (module plate / circular node / REF.0x label) visually distinct.
Do use the single Flat Offset shadow for elevation; don't reach for blur or colored glow.
Do treat this file as a captured baseline open to further reinvention per PRODUCT.md.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color alongside safety orange, or reintroduce the old cyan/amber pair.
Don't add gradient text anywhere — the previous system's one exception (step-number) was removed in this redesign.
Don't add backdrop-filter/blur chrome anywhere; it was removed from the topbar and hero stage.
Don't nest cards inside cards, or default to the vertical-card grid for every new content group.
Don't let the bubble/spark particle layer become permanent visual chrome.
